To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) response-independent reinforcements can enhance the persistence of response-dependent reinforcements and (b) the reinforcements do not have to the same to produce this effect.

(a) response-independent reinforcements enhance the persistence of response-independent reinforcemnts, and (b) this enhancement is greater when the reinforcers are of larger magnitude and when there is more time between the components.

(a) the response-independent reinforcer does not have to be identical to the response-dependent reinforcer to produce a response-strengthening effect and (b) the response-independent reinforcement effect is enhanced by increasing the size of the response-independent reinforer and increasing the time that the response-independent and response-dependent reinforcerns are separated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of response-independent reinforcements (RIRs) on the persistence of lever pressing by rats (see, for example, Brown & Jenkins, 1968; Dallery & Silverman, 1998).
how the delivery schedule of response-independent reinforcements affects the persistence of a lever-pressing response.
understanding the conditions under which response-reinforcer independence will enhance persistence of lever pressing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
response-dependent and response-independent reinforcements are not necessary to enhance persistence.

, in the presence and absence of response-independent reinforcements, the size and the temporal distribution of the response-independent reinforcer(s) are important variables that can influence the persistence of response-dependent behavior.
the response-independent reinforcer must be the same type of reinforcer as the response-dependent one in order to enhance the response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
persistence is enhanced by the presentation of a signal that has been correlated, in the past, with a higher-than-usual rate of reinforcement.

the persistence of a response reinforced by a single type of reinforcer is enhanced when (a) a second type of reinforcer, independent of the response, is correlated with one of two stimuli, (b) the second reinforcer is delivered in larger amounts, and (c) components are separated by blackouts.

response-independent reinforcments enhance the resistance to extinction of the response that was correlated with them during training, and that the magnitude of the enhancement is a direct function of the magnitude of the response-independent reinforcer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order for the response-independent reinforcer to enhance persistence, the response-independent reinforer must be delivered at a high rate and the response-dependent reinforcer must be delivered at low rate.
the size of the response-independent reinforcer and the duration of the blackout separating components may influence persistence of lever pressing.
, in order to enhance persistence of responding, response-independent reinforcments should be large, and the components should be separated by long blackouts.
